dropped.finding: MCP wire output contract narrowed: optional result keys that clients could previously read as an explicit `null` (e.g. `cross_session_warning`, `last_reopened_at`, `source_id`/`source_created_at`/`source_author`/`source_env`, write-ack `push_status.*` sub-keys, lean `list_tickets` row fields) are now ABSENT when unset because tool bodies return the raw library dict and the pydantic mirror that re-added `null` defaults was deleted. A client reading these keys with subscript access (`row['cross_session_warning']`) rather than `.get` will raise KeyError.
scenarios: An MCP client that indexes an optional result key directly (not via `.get`) after upgrading the rebar MCP server

dropped.finding: test_every_advertised_output_schema_equals_its_canonical_file asserts `advertised == inline_schema(names, kind)` — comparing the installed outputSchema against the very function the installer used to build it (a convergence twin). For `array`/`list_of` tools this assertion is the only oracle in THIS test; the independent raw-file comparison on lines 60-67 runs only for `kind == "object"`, so a bug in inline_schema's list/array wrapping or common-def hoisting would not be caught by this test (it is caught by the separate real-wire validation tests, so the gap is advisory).
scenarios: A regression in inline_schema's list_of/array wrapping (e.g. mis-shaped `{"result": {...}}` or dropped `anyOf`) would leave this test green.
